BLOCKER_1a_frontend_skill_soft_row.was: an UNCONDITIONAL instruction: premium/luxury/calm/expensive/elegant/glossy surfaces — pair with a high-craft Layer B (supabase, linear.app, vercel, stripe).
BLOCKER_1a_frontend_skill_soft_row.now: conditioned on `when the user named NO brand (greenfield)`, and it closes the other branch explicitly: `this row never licenses a substitute brand: a brand the user NAMED that the catalogue lacks gets this Layer A mood match ALONE, never another brand's tokens (see the Layer B section)`.
BLOCKER_1a_frontend_skill_soft_row.why_this_is_the_fix: the same file already stated the named-brand rule two paragraphs later (the Layer B section, line 76) and in the Phase-2 greenfield bullet (line 37); the table row was the one place an agent reading top-down hit the pairing FIRST and unconditionally. The two statements are now additive instead of contradictory.

BLOCKER_1b_design_readme_step2_mood_row.was: `soft-skill.md` + a high-craft Layer B (supabase / linear.app / vercel / stripe) for the whole premium/luxury/glossy mood row — no brand condition.
BLOCKER_1b_design_readme_step2_mood_row.now: `soft-skill.md`, plus a high-craft Layer B ONLY when the user named NO brand (greenfield). A brand the user NAMED that this catalogue lacks keeps `soft-skill.md` as a Layer A mood match ALONE — never another brand's tokens.
BLOCKER_1b_design_readme_step2_mood_row.why_this_is_the_fix: Step 2's prose (line 113) was already scoped this way in the previous round while its own table still said the opposite; an agent that skips prose and reads the table got the leak. The table now matches the prose.

BLOCKER_1c_design_readme_concrete_refere.was: `You may also load a brand DESIGN.md from Layer B as a *concrete reference* if the user's mood maps cleanly` — and this same file defines a loaded reference as SOURCE MATERIAL whose tokens are extracted, so the sentence licensed another brand's tokens for a mere mood.
BLOCKER_1c_design_readme_concrete_refere.now: `as a *concrete reference* — source material whose tokens you extract — only when the user named NO brand and the mood maps cleanly`. That latitude never covers a brand the user NAMED: a named brand's OWN catalogue file is the only Layer B token source, and when the catalogue lacks it the output is a Layer A mood match alone, never another brand's tokens.
BLOCKER_1c_design_readme_concrete_refere.why_this_is_the_fix: this was the widest of the three: it did not merely suggest a pairing, it authorised loading a SUBSTITUTE brand file as token truth. Scoping it to the no-brand case removes the last route by which a named-but-absent brand could end up wearing another brand's palette.
